text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Advance voting at post offices began on Wednesday in Finland's local government and European Parliament elections, with more people voting for local councillors than Euro-MPs.
- Visiting Greek President Costis Stephanopoulos sharply criticised the EU, saying ex-Yugoslav crisis displayed lack of coherent foreign policy.
- A group of 20 translators from several countries gathered to translate Bible into the more exotic Fenno-Ugric languages.
- Police say Finnish Hells' Angels have extensive network of criminal support gangs across the country.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Shortage of building sites threatens to hinder recovery in house construction.
- Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said that growth of even four percent next year would not be impossible.
- Poyry group unit Maa ja Vesi Oy clinched order for environmental project in Egypt.
- Valmet Automotive planning to build car factory in Russia.
- Remodelled Sokos department store opens doors today -- aims for annual net sales of 500 million markka by 2000.
- Nordic environmental groups critical of Finland's new energy tax and call for Nordic cooperation.
DEMARI
- Proposed reform of state regional administration to create five big provinces has backing of only a slim majority in parliament and opponents in all parties.
- Author Jorn Donner says he and social democrat MP Markus Aaltonen came up with idea of getting Martti Ahtisaari to run for president over a beer at South African airport in 1989.
AAMULEHTI
- Western Finland region of Hame has civil defence shelters for fewer than half the area's inhabitants.
- Police have introduced new high-precision breathalysers to check drivers in Helsinki and Lahti.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Wartsila Diesel has begun expansion of Turku factory.
- Almost 70,000 Finns living in Sweden are entitled to vote in European Parliament elections on October 20.
